parts.title: Fathers and Sons
lines: When we hear the word “respect,” we often think of it as something external — rules of behavior, politeness, or the right words to say in certain situations. It seems that if we aren't rude, don't interrupt and keep a polite distance, that's already enough. But no, respect isn't only about behavior — it's about attitude. It's about the ability to see a person in someone else,
With their own experience, their own views, their own feelings. Respect shows in how we listen, how we react,

How we accept what doesn't match our own point of view. Because to respect doesn't mean to agree. It means recognizing another person's right to be different. And in a world so full of arguments and attempts to prove we're right, it is respect that lets people understand instead of destroy. Because without respect there can be no trust,
No dialogue, no real connection. And perhaps respect begins with one simple thought: in front of you is not just someone you're talking to, but a person whose life matters just as much as yours.

parts.title: My Music
lines: Every person has music they can never fully explain to anyone else. You can say who wrote it, translate the lyrics, show the chords, but none of that conveys the main thing — the feeling that rises inside when the first notes begin. My music has never been just background. It arrived exactly in those moments when words were too small for my thoughts. When something important is happening inside a person, music somehow begins to speak for them. It knows how to live through with us what we ourselves can't always express. There are songs that take us back to the past faster than any photograph. One familiar melody is enough, and suddenly streets, people, conversations, scents and evenings that seemed long gone come back to life. Music is strange that way: it keeps our emotions more precisely than memory does. Sometimes a single song can support a person better than a hundred pieces of advice. Because music doesn't try to fix us. It simply, honestly stays by our side. In joy, in loneliness, on the road, at night, when the city outside has long since fallen asleep and you keep thinking about something of your own.

And that's probably why people will never stop making music. As long as a person feels, they will search for a sound that can pass that feeling on to someone else. First there were drums beaten around an ancient fire, then came orchestras, vinyl, headphones, digital platforms, but the essence stayed the same: music has always been our attempt to tell the world what ordinary words can't say. My music isn't a genre or a list of favorite songs. It's a part of my inner world that, every now and then, fills up.

parts.title: My Favorite Film
lines: Everyone has a film they can watch again and again. Years go by, new movies come out, tastes change, but that one film stays special. Why? Because a good film is much more than just a story on a screen. A favorite film can carry us into other worlds. In a couple of hours we can find ourselves in the distant future, set off on a dangerous journey, solve a mysterious crime or live someone else's life alongside the characters. We laugh with them, feel their failures and celebrate their victories as if it were all happening to us. But the true value of cinema isn't only entertainment. Good films make us think. They remind us of friendship, love, courage and staying true to our principles. Sometimes a single scene or a single line can stay with us for years and even change the way we see the world. A favorite film also becomes part of our lives because it's tied to memories. Maybe we first watched it with our family, with friends, or at a moment that will always stay dear to our hearts. And every time we watch it again, it brings back not only the plot, but the feelings we once had. That's why a favorite film is never just a film. It's a story that once found its way into our hearts and stayed there forever.

parts.title: WI-FI
lines: In today's world, media have become much more than a source of information or entertainment — they are a powerful force that quietly shapes how we see ourselves, because every day we see hundreds of images, perfect faces, successful lives and edited realities, and little by little, without even noticing, we start comparing our lives to what may really be just a pretty picture. We begin to wonder: are we good enough, successful enough, attractive enough — when in fact we're comparing ourselves not to reality, but to a carefully assembled image that rarely leaves room for mistakes, weaknesses and ordinary human moments.

And that is the real danger — losing our sense of self-worth, forgetting that real life doesn't have to look perfect to be genuine and meaningful. So perhaps the most important task is not to let outside noise drown out our inner voice, to learn to tell reality from illusion, and to remember that self-esteem shouldn't be built on other people's pictures, but should grow from understanding our own uniqueness, our own path, and our real, imperfect, but truly alive selves.

parts.title: The Bond Between Generations
lines: Sometimes it feels like the world is changing too fast. New technologies appear before we've gotten used to the old ones, cities grow, habits change, and time seems to run faster and faster. But there is something that stays the same in every era — the bond between generations. No one comes into this world empty-handed. Along with a name, each of us receives the history of our family, its traditions, memories, values and experience. We learn to speak thanks to our parents, we learn about kindness and fairness thanks to our elders, we take on their wisdom without even noticing how their words become part of our character. Generations are like links in one long chain. Remove even a single link, and the chain loses its strength. In the same way, a society can't exist without respect for the past and care for the future. The elders pass on their knowledge, and the young bring new ideas. Progress is born from this exchange. The bond between generations isn't only family photos in albums and stories about the past. It's the ability to listen to each other, to understand different views and to preserve the best of what was created before us. After all, one day we will be the people whose experience the next generations will need. And perhaps our most important task is to make sure that many years from now our children and grandchildren can proudly say: “We remember those who came before us, and we carry on their path.”

parts.title: AI
lines: People once dreamed of machines that could understand human speech, answer questions and help solve difficult problems. For a long time such ideas existed only on the pages of science fiction novels. Today they've become part of everyday life. Artificial intelligence quietly surrounds us every day. It helps us find information, translate texts, plan routes, recommend music and even take part in scientific discoveries. What seemed unbelievable not long ago is gradually becoming an ordinary tool. Yet artificial intelligence is fascinating not only for what it can do. Its development makes humanity take a fresh look at its own nature. What makes a human different from a machine? The ability to feel? To create? To show compassion? Or the ability to make decisions where there's no ready-made answer? The more advanced technology becomes, the more often such questions arise. And it's important to remember: every algorithm is created by people. Behind every program stand the ideas of engineers, scientists, researchers and dreamers. Machines can process enormous amounts of data, but it is people who decide which way they go. Whether new technologies benefit society depends on human responsibility. The history of civilization has always been a history of inventions. The wheel, the printing press, electricity, the internet — each discovery changed the world. Artificial intelligence is the next page of that story. And how it continues depends not only on what technology can do, but on the wisdom of those who use it.

parts.title: Connection
lines: A person rarely takes shape alone, because our views, habits, behavior and even thoughts are largely shaped by the people we spend the most time with, the conversations we hear, and the atmosphere we live in every day. Our surroundings can quietly push us to grow, inspire us to develop, support us in a hard moment — or, on the contrary, hold us back, make us doubt ourselves and stop us from moving forward.
And the hardest part is that this influence isn't always obvious, because it happens gradually — through small things, through familiar words, through situations that repeat.
Because in the long run, the people around you become a part of you.

parts.title: Contemplation
lines: Sometimes we're in such a hurry to live that we forget to ask: are we actually living at all?
The days fly by. Tasks, to-dos, worries. And it seems like real life is somewhere “later” — when things get easier. When there's more time. When everything is perfect.
“Later” is a very dangerous word.
Because life is happening now. In simple moments. In laughing with friends.
In your favorite music. In sunsets we sometimes don't even look at.
Living life to the fullest isn't about something grand.
It's about the ability to notice, to feel, to enjoy.
To stop for a moment and realize: “I feel good. Right now.”
Not to wait for a special day, but to make ordinary days special. Because that's exactly what life is made of.
And perhaps the most important thing is to remember, now and then, to simply stop, take a deep breath and feel that you are alive. Truly alive.

parts.title: The Idea
lines: Every great undertaking begins with something almost invisible. Not with loud speeches, not with huge fortunes, not with worldwide fame. It all begins with an idea — a tiny spark that one day appears in someone's mind. At first glance, an idea has no weight, no shape and no price. You can't hold it in your hands or measure it with a ruler. And yet it is ideas that cause the greatest changes. They turn into books, paintings, discoveries, companies, cities and even entire eras. Everyone has had that moment at least once, when a thought arrives completely out of the blue: on a walk, in a conversation, while reading. Such moments are like a flash of light in a dark room. Suddenly you see familiar things in a new way, and what seemed impossible just recently begins to take real shape. Of course, an idea alone isn't enough. Between the plan and the result lies a road that demands patience, hard work and persistence. Many good ideas remain dreams simply because no one dared to take the first step. And the boldest achievements of humanity came from people who believed in their own thought and found the strength to bring it to life. The world keeps changing thanks to those who dare to think differently. That's why it's worth taking your ideas seriously. You can never know in advance which one of them will someday become the beginning of something truly significant. Because great changes are often born from one simple thought that someone, at some point, refused to forget.

parts.title: A Clean Slate
lines: We're used to thinking that a mistake is a bad thing.
Something to be avoided. A sign of weakness or failure.
The truth is, mistakes are part of every journey.
No one becomes strong without making mistakes.
No success comes without attempts that didn't work.
So why is it that, as we grow older, we start to fear mistakes?
We're afraid of looking foolish. Afraid of being judged. Afraid that we won't succeed.
A mistake isn't the end. It's a hint.
It shows you where you can get better. Where you need to try once more.
If you see mistakes not as failures but as experience, they'll stop scaring you and start helping you. And the biggest mistake of all is never trying.

parts.title: The Artist and His Creation
lines: So.

Look at a blank canvas. It's silent. White, smooth, completely indifferent to the world. And then a person with a brush walks up to it. What does he do? He argues with emptiness. He throws the first stroke onto the white, and from that moment the canvas no longer belongs to silence. Now it belongs to the artist. And do you know the secret? An artist doesn't paint what he sees. He paints what he feels. His tree can be blue, his sky green, and a human face assembled from a thousand fragments, like Picasso's. And we believe it. We stand before the painting and recognize ourselves in it, even though there's not a single familiar feature. A creation outlives its creator. The artist grows old, falls ill, passes away. But the stroke he laid down at thirty, with a hand trembling with inspiration, stays fresh four centuries later. The paint remembers a movement that no longer exists. That's why I take my hat off to everyone who picks up a brush. It takes courage bordering on audacity. To take color, form and light and tell the world: look, this is how I saw it. And the world looks, and remembers.

parts.title: Technologies of the Future
lines: Once, people dreamed of flying as they watched the birds. Today we complain about a delayed flight while sitting in a seat ten thousand meters up.

That's what the future is: it arrives and instantly becomes ordinary. Let's be honest. The future is already here — it's just not evenly distributed. Somewhere a neural network writes music, makes diagnoses, paints portraits. And somewhere else a person is still looking for an outlet to charge their phone. Future technologies frighten and fascinate us at the same time. A machine learns to understand our speech. A prosthetic limb obeys the power of thought. A car drives itself while the driver looks out the window, like a passenger in his own life. But let me tell you one thing that's easy to forget among all these wonders. Every technology, even the most advanced, is born from a deeply human desire. The desire to live longer. To see further. To be closer to the ones we love, even when there's an ocean between us. So when someone shows you a robot or a talking program, don't ask how smart it is. Ask whether it makes us kinder. Because the future isn't built by a processor. The future is built by us.

parts.title: Freedom of Speech
lines: There are things in this world you can't hold in your hands, slip into your pocket or lock away in a safe, and yet they are worth more than gold, and the freedom to say what you think is made of exactly that rare, almost weightless substance — the one for which, through the centuries, people went out to the squares, climbed the scaffold and wrote their finest lines by the light of a dying candle. Imagine a world where every word must first pass inspection, be weighed on someone's invisible scales and allowed to live only with permission, and you'll feel how quiet, stifling and empty such a world becomes, because a person stripped of the right to their own voice slowly forgets even how to think, since a thought that is forbidden to be spoken eventually becomes afraid to be born at all. And yet freedom of speech doesn't mean the freedom to shout anything at anyone, forgetting that every word has weight, temperature and consequences, because the true maturity of a speaker shows not in being able to say everything, but in choosing to say what matters, to say it honestly, and to say it so that people hear it, not merely fear it. Guard this right the way you guard your own breath, because silence that is forced on you and silence that you choose are two completely different silences, and only a people who can speak openly can also openly love, argue, build, and remain truly alive.

parts.title: What Is Marketing
lines: In today's world, media have become an inseparable part of our lives, shaping not only what we see and hear but also how we see ourselves, because every day we face a huge number of images, stories and standards that create a certain idea of what a person “should” be. We see perfect photos, success stories, bright moments, and little by little we start comparing ourselves to this flood of information, forgetting that behind these images there is often an edited reality where you can't see the doubts, the mistakes and the ordinary human struggles. And this is exactly where the risk lies — starting to measure our worth by someone else's standards. We may feel we're not good enough,

Not successful enough, not measuring up. But if we stop and think, it becomes clear that self-esteem can't be built on comparison with something that isn't the whole reality. Because every person has their own path,
Their own pace, their own strengths. And perhaps the most important thing is to learn to filter what we see,
And not let outside noise define our inner worth. Because that worth doesn't depend on pictures — it grows from understanding yourself.

parts.title: Humor Is Medicine
lines: Of all the remedies humanity has invented over its long and sometimes unbearably serious history, there is one that has no color and no scent, isn't sold in any pharmacy, and yet heals where every potion fails — the ability to laugh, that very laughter which in a single second can melt the ice between strangers and bring hope back to someone who had almost stopped waiting for it. Notice how this remarkable mechanism works: a person weighed down by worries, bent under the burden of the day, suddenly hears a witty joke, and his shoulders straighten, the line on his forehead smooths out, and his eyes, dull just a minute ago, light up again with the glow we call an interest in life — and all of it happens without pills, without prescriptions, completely free of charge. Humor is also good because it doesn't deny grief or pretend that trouble doesn't exist; it simply takes trouble by the hand and leads it into the light, letting us look at our own misfortunes from a little higher up, from that saving height where even the gloomiest problem suddenly turns out to be not as huge as it seemed a minute ago in the dark. And so I wish each of you to keep this wonderful gift close, not to lose it in the bustle and not to trade it for grim self-importance, because whoever can laugh at themselves is truly invincible, and a home where laughter lives will always be warmer, brighter and stronger than any other.

parts.title: Learning Is Light
lines: Since the most ancient times, when the first human picked up a piece of charcoal from the ground and drew a timid line on a cave wall, trying to preserve for his descendants what he had learned about the beast, the stars and himself, this quiet and endless relay began, in which knowledge is passed from palm to palm, from lips to lips, from one generation to the next weary one, like a carefully guarded fire that must not go out in any storm. Think of the miracle contained in a single open book: a person who left this world long ago, whose bones have turned to dust and whose name has sometimes been erased from the memory of the ages, keeps speaking to you across the centuries, sharing hard-won wisdom, arguing, comforting and leading you on — and so a diligent student is never alone, for behind his shoulder stands an unseen army of teachers from ages past. Ignorance, on the other hand, is like a room with boarded-up windows, where a person gropes his way along cold walls, bumping into corners and mistaking his own fears for monsters, while every ray that breaks through a crack of knowledge doesn't just scatter the darkness, but shows the lost one that there is a way out, that the world is far wider and kinder than it seemed to him in the dark. So reach for the light of the mind all your life, never thinking yourself too grown-up for a new lesson or too wise to be amazed, because whoever stops learning begins to slowly fade while still alive, and whoever keeps in their heart the thirst to understand and to know stays young and burning bright until their very last day.

parts.title: Speak About Your Dream
lines: When we talk about dreams, they often seem like something distant and unreal, like beautiful images that don't always have much to do with real life. We may think that dreams are just wishes,
Pleasant to imagine, but not necessarily meant to come true. But in fact, dreams play a much more important role. They set the direction. They give meaning to our efforts.

They create a sense of moving forward. Because a person without a dream often starts living on autopilot, repeating the same actions without ever asking “why.” But a person who has a dream, even a distant one,

Is already moving. They see a goal. They make choices. They try. And even if the road turns out harder than expected, the dream itself keeps giving them energy. So perhaps dreams aren't only meant to come true. They're meant to keep us walking. And to let us feel that our life
Has a direction.

parts.title: Movement
lines: In a world where everything keeps speeding up and where we're taught to compare results, achievements and pace, it's very easy to start believing that only speed has value, that what matters is to come first, faster than others, faster than yesterday, faster than people expect, but in this race the most important thing often gets lost — the movement itself.
Because speed only matters once you're already heading in the right direction, and if you're standing still, even the most perfect conditions and plans won't lead to any result.

Sometimes a person takes slow steps, doubts, stops, keeps going again, and from the outside it may look like uncertainty, but in fact this is exactly where growth happens, where experience is formed and understanding appears.
And the other way around, a fast start without awareness can lead a person to simply burn out or take a wrong turn. So what matters is not how fast you go,
But that you don't stop. Because movement, even slow movement, always takes you further than perfect speed without action.

parts.title: Sport Is Life
lines: Watch a runner one day at the end of the race, when his lungs are burning, his legs are turning to lead, and only a few agonizing meters remain to the finish line, and in that single moment you'll see the whole of human destiny in miniature, for right there, at the very edge of strength, the question is not who is faster, but who can take one more step when the body begs to stop. That is the first great lesson of sport: it doesn't promise easy victory and doesn't trade in comfort, but honestly shows each of us what we're made of, making us fall and get up, lose and lace up our sneakers again the next morning, and in this daily duel with our own weakness we forge a character far stronger than that of someone who has never tested their limits. Sport has a second gift, just as generous, because a stadium unites complete strangers faster than any speeches or treaties, turning a crowd of many voices into one heart that freezes and rejoices in a single rhythm, and in those minutes it doesn't matter where you come from, how much you have or what you believe, because the joy of a shared victory erases all the borders that the rest of life so carefully builds. So move, dare, challenge your own laziness and fatigue, because as long as the heart beats and the muscles obey, a human being is made not to sink into an armchair, but to jump higher than they thought possible, to reach for the unreachable and to prove, above all to themselves, that a living, breathing life that keeps surging forward is the highest reward of all.

parts.title: Creativity Is Irreplaceable
lines: You can build a machine that calculates faster than a thousand sages, you can teach a mechanism to lift the unliftable and repeat the same motion millions of times without tiring or complaining, but no device, however ingenious, will ever feel that sweet shiver that runs down a person's spine at the moment when, out of nothing, out of thin air and a vague hunch, something is suddenly born in their mind that never existed in the world before. That is where the great secret lies: all true creativity is a daring argument with emptiness, the attempt of a mortal being to leave its own signature on the indifferent face of eternity, and so the artist bent over a canvas, the poet catching a slipping line, the child shaping a lopsided animal out of clay are all, in essence, doing the same noble work — turning nothingness into beauty. Notice, too, that the fruits of someone else's inspiration don't take our strength away but generously add to it, for a melody we hear awakens feelings in our chest that have long been asleep, a novel we read gives us a whole life lived in one evening, and a painting we see can reconcile us with the world at an hour when we wanted to run from it, and this whole invisible exchange of warmth obeys no laws of trade. So guard the spark of the creator within you, as you would guard your last match in a frozen forest, don't let the bustle and calculation burn out your ability to wonder and invent, because that is what separates living from merely existing, and as long as a person creates, however clumsily, even if only for themselves, they remain an irreplaceable link in that shining chain that stretches from the first cave painting to the masterpieces of the future yet to be written.

parts.title: The Vast World Around Us
lines: All it takes is to truly lift your head, just once, from the familiar path between home and work, to look up from the flicker of everyday worries, and you're hit by a stunning feeling, as if all your life you'd been reading a single page of an enormous book, never suspecting that thousands more await beyond it, full of seas you've never crossed, languages in which you've never said a word, and sunsets fading right now over cities whose names you don't even know. Imagine for a moment that right this second, while you're listening to me, somewhere a fisherman in a fragile boat is pulling his net out of a warm ocean, a caravan is trudging through scorching sands, a child is seeing snow for the first time and laughing in amazement, and on the other side of the earth a weary traveler is falling asleep under the stars, and all these countless lives are flowing at the same time, weaving together into one gigantic tapestry, and you and I are a small patch of it. The great sorrow and the great happiness of being human lie precisely in this: the world is immeasurably bigger than any of us, it can't be taken in by the eye, by memory, or by the longest road, and yet that's no reason to give up, because it's this very vastness that calls us onto the road, teases our imagination and keeps the heart from hardening — the heart that has grown used to measuring the universe by the size of its own room. So open your eyes and your soul wide to this boundlessness, talk to people who are unlike you, try the unfamiliar, go where no one is expecting you, because life is given to us not to wear a single path down to a shine, but to touch, if only at the edge, the dazzling diversity of the earth and carry away a sense of wonder that can't be bought and can't be forgotten.

parts.title: The Power of Love
lines: Of all the driving forces that for centuries have pushed people toward madness and heroic deeds, made them cross oceans, compose immortal lines and do things they would never dare in a sober mind even under threat of death, there is nothing mightier than this quiet flame, which doesn't clash like weapons or thunder like commands, but simply burns in the chest, steady and tireless, turning around the fates of whole nations and of a single quiet heart. The very nature of this feeling is astonishing, because it obeys neither calculation, nor logic, nor the arguments of caution: a mother throws herself into fire for her child without hesitation, a gray-haired old man stays faithful to the one whose face time smoothed away long ago, and yesterday's egoist, the moment he falls in love, suddenly discovers he's ready to give his last and to see it not as a sacrifice but as an unexpected gift, and in such a miraculous transformation you can see the full transforming power of love. It heals where doctors give up, lifts up the fallen who've already been told they'll never rise, and often turns out to be the only thread that held a person back at the edge, because knowing that somewhere in the world there beats a heart to which you are dear can matter more than bread and be stronger than any armor, and this invisible thread is sometimes stretched across entire continents without losing a single drop of its strength. So don't be stingy with it, don't hide it behind a mask of pride and don't put off a warm word until later — a later that has the treacherous habit of never coming — because a life in which you loved and were loved was not lived in vain, however short and hard it turned out to be, and a heart that generously gave its warmth remains, until its very last beat, immeasurably richer than a chest stuffed full of gold.

parts.title: Back to the Future
lines: There is a special kind of dizziness in the simple thought that time carries us forward without stopping, never asking our consent and never letting us pull over to catch our breath, and yet the human being, alone among all living things, is gifted with the strange ability to remember the road behind and dream of what hasn't yet come, as if standing on the crest of a wave, facing the past while feeling the breath of the future on the back of the neck. See how curiously these two elements are woven together in us: we reach for the new, we dream of cities under domes and ships among the stars, and at the same time we carefully keep in the pockets of our memory the smell of grandma's house, the tune of an old song, the warmth of a cup that went cold long ago — which means you can't truly step forward without planting your foot on the solid ground of everything that came before us and made us who we are. That is the wisdom not everyone arrives at: the future is built not by rejecting the past, but by having an honest conversation with it, for a people who have forgotten their roots are like a tree with its roots cut — it stays green for a while out of habit, but it is already doomed, while whoever honors past generations draws from them the strength for daring leaps into places their ancestors never even dreamed of setting foot. So let's move forward without burning bridges behind us and without fouling the well our grandfathers drank from, let's take on the long road all the best that the centuries have gathered, leaving by the roadside only old grudges and outworn fears, because only someone who looks back on yesterday with gratitude can face tomorrow with true courage, carrying its light like a torch into the distance that is not yet lit.

parts.title: A Hero of Our Time
lines: Sometimes it seems to us that the world is something too big, too complex and too far beyond one person's control to even try to change anything in it. We look at global problems, at millions of people, at enormous cities, and we think our voice is just a drop that decides nothing. But if we think a little deeper, any big world is actually made of small stories, of individual people, of actions that at first seem insignificant.
Every change that has ever happened began with one person who didn't wait for someone else to take the first step.
With a person who one day decided to speak up, to make a choice, to reach out a hand, to support, to try — in spite of doubt and fear.
And perhaps at that moment they didn't think they were changing the world either —

They were simply doing what they believed was right. But it's exactly these decisions that start a chain reaction. One action influences another person, that person influences the next, and gradually it becomes something bigger than the action of one. The world doesn't change all at once or loudly. It changes quietly, gradually, through people who don't walk on by.
And in that sense, every person truly matters. Not because they have to change everything at once,
But because they can change something.
Sometimes that something, small as it seems at first glance, is already the beginning of something enormous.
The most important question isn't whether you can change the whole world, but whether you're ready to change at least a small part of it.

parts.title: A Rising Star
lines: When we hear the word “success,” we often picture something big, bright and visible — achievements, recognition, victories that everyone around can see. It seems to us that success must be something loud and measurable, something you can show, prove and compare with others.
But if you stop and honestly ask yourself, it becomes clear that success looks different for every person.
For some, it really is big goals and ambitions, and for others it's a quiet feeling that they're walking their own road and not betraying themselves.
Sometimes success isn't the moment when people applaud you, but the moment when you didn't give up even though it was hard. When you keep going, even if no one notices.
When you choose yourself, your values, your dreams, even if it isn't the easiest path. Real success is rarely instant.
It's built from small steps, from decisions, from days when you choose to move forward despite fatigue, doubt and fear.
And the most interesting part is that from the outside it may look like an ordinary life.
But inside, it's enormous work, enormous growth, enormous strength. So perhaps success isn't about how far you've gone,
But about how honestly you've walked your path. And if one day you can tell yourself: “I'm trying, I'm not giving up, I'm living the way I believe is right” —
Then you're already closer to your success than you think.

parts.title: My Choice
lines: Every morning we wake up with countless possibilities, and although it seems the world dictates its rules and directions to us,
In reality it is we who decide who we'll be today, what words we'll say, what actions we'll take, and even the smallest choice can have consequences that become part of our story;

Because life isn't a series of accidents but a chain of decisions, and if we stop being afraid to choose, stop waiting for someone else to show us the way, we'll begin to steer our own destiny, we'll taste freedom and responsibility at the same time,
And in that moment we'll understand that real strength was always inside us — we were just afraid to believe in it.

parts.title: The Power of Words
lines: Responsibility is often seen as a duty, as something heavy and limiting, a set of rules and demands that have to be followed. It may seem that responsibility is about pressure, about control, about a lack of freedom. But if we look deeper, it becomes clear

That responsibility is, on the contrary, a sign of maturity and strength. It's the ability to admit that your decisions have consequences. That your actions affect not only you, but the people around you. It's the ability not to shift the blame,
Not to look for excuses,
But to accept reality as it is. And most importantly, it's the readiness to act

Based on that understanding. Responsibility doesn't limit freedom. It makes freedom conscious. Because only by understanding the consequences does a person truly choose. Perhaps this is what a truly grown-up attitude means — not avoiding responsibility,
But embracing it as part of your strength.

parts.title: Millennials
lines: Dear friends, it's great to see you.

You know, there's one word we've been hearing literally everywhere in recent years — “millennials.” People say it in different tones: some with irony, some with reproach, and some with open bewilderment.

This generation grew up at the crossroads of two worlds — without the internet and with it. They remember a time when you had to search for information, and they live in a world where it comes to you on its own. And perhaps that's exactly why they ask more questions: “Why am I doing this?”, “Do I really need this?”, “Is this even my life?”

They're often criticized for choosing what interests them over what they “should” do. But is it really bad to want to work where you find meaning, not just a steady paycheck? Is it really weakness to walk away from something that doesn't suit you?

It seems to me that what we're seeing isn't a problem, but a change in the rules. The world has become different, and people have become different. And perhaps in a few years, what seems strange today will become the new normal.
So the next time you hear the word “millennials,” try to see it not as a label, but as a sign that time really is changing right before our eyes.
Thank you.

parts.title: Life's Work
lines: When we talk about success, we often picture talent, luck or inspiration, but we think much less often about what stands behind those results — the everyday actions that aren't always visible, yet they are what shape the outcome.

Self-discipline isn't about harshness or restrictions; it's about the ability to do what needs to be done even when you're not in the mood, when it's hard, when you want to put it off or give up. It's the ability to keep your focus on the goal without being distracted by passing desires that bring quick comfort but don't lead to lasting results.
It is self-discipline that turns intentions into actions,
And actions into results.
Because motivation comes and goes,
But the habit of acting stays. And perhaps the main secret of success isn't always wanting to do something, but doing it even when you don't want to.

parts.title: Legacy and Art
lines: Think for a moment about how little remains of a person once their days have run their course: the body is given to the earth, belongings scatter into other hands, the voice falls silent, and even the loudest fame of a lifetime melts away like a boot print on wet sand that the next tide licks away without a trace, and only one thing proves immune to this universal dissolving — what a person managed to put into the work of their own hands and soul. Look closely at any ancient fresco, at a statue darkened by the centuries, at a line written by a hand that long ago turned to dust: a nameless master, of whom neither a date of birth nor the sound of a voice remains, still moves us more deeply than many of the living, because into his work he sealed a particle of living warmth, and that warmth, like embers beneath a layer of ash, hasn't cooled over the millennia and still warms anyone who leans over it with an open heart. That is the greatness of art: it turns a fragile, mortal, forgetful human being into a link in an endless roll call, where each generation leaves its descendants a message about what it felt, what it feared and what it loved, and our whole history appears not as a string of empty names in a textbook, but as a living conversation across the depths of time that never broke off, not in the days of plague, nor under the thunder of wars. So leave behind a worthy legacy, not of stone alone and not of bronze, but of deeds filled with truth and beauty, because sooner or later each of us will have to go, and the only question truly worth asking yourself in this life is not how much we took from the world, but what we managed to give it that is destined to outlive us and light the way for those who follow.

parts.title: The Path of Humanity
lines: Cast your mind's eye over the whole incredible road our kind has traveled, from that distant night when an ancestor, trembling with fear, huddled by a timid fire, surrounded on all sides by darkness, roaring beasts and mysteries he had neither name nor reason for, to this very day, when the descendants of that same creature gaze at the edges of the universe and split the invisible nucleus, and you can't help but be struck with wonder at the stubbornness with which humanity has climbed out of darkness toward the light. This road has never been straight or easy; it twisted, broke off into chasms, led into dead ends of cruelty and delusion, and how many times it seemed that all was lost, that savagery would win and the fire of reason would go out forever, and yet time after time someone was found who raised the fallen banner, who saved a grain of knowledge in troubled times and passed it on, never letting the thinnest thread of continuity snap. And the most heartening thing in this long chronicle is that, for all the setbacks and falls, the overall movement has steadily led us upward — from the club to the word, from revenge to justice, from a tribe that saw a stranger as prey to the dream of one family of nations, and even if we still have a long, long way to go to reach that dream, the very fact that it lives in the human heart shows that we are capable of becoming better than we were yesterday. So let us neither boast of what we've achieved nor give up in the face of the world's imperfection, but take up our share of the common load and carry it on with dignity, remembering that we are not spectators on this great journey but its rightful participants, and how we spend our own short stretch of it will decide what kind of dawn awaits those who come after us and one day ask what we lived for and what we left behind.

parts.title: Tomorrow
lines: There is something truly magical in this one simple word, because tomorrow exists nowhere but in our imagination; you can't touch it, see it or claim it in advance, and yet it is tomorrow, elusive and not yet born, that keeps almost every one of us afloat in the darkest hours, whispering a stubborn promise that everything can still change if only we hold on until dawn. Think how many people in despair have been kept going by nothing more than the hope of seeing how tomorrow turns out: a patient clings to it in a hospital ward, a mother waits for her son to return from far away, someone who has lost everything starts over from scratch, and what unites them all is an instinctive belief that the coming day doesn't have to repeat today, that fate has turns in store we can't even imagine while we sort through our present troubles in the dark. But tomorrow has a tricky quality: it doesn't arrive ready-made and all arranged, it's quietly assembled from what we do, or are too lazy to do, right now, and every action we take today, every word we say and every decision we make quietly lays another brick in the wall of the house we're going to wake up in, whether we want it or not. So meet tomorrow not as a gift from outside that will simply fall from the sky, but as a field plowed by your own hands today; sow it with what is good and wise, and don't be afraid that it won't sprout right away, because the future, by rights, belongs not to those who wait for it passively by the window, but to those who patiently and persistently prepare a worthy welcome for it, believing that the best is yet to come — and that it depends, above all, on ourselves.

parts.title: In the Spotlight
lines: The need for recognition is one of the deepest human needs, because everyone wants to feel seen, heard and valued, to know that their efforts matter and don't go unnoticed. From early childhood, a person looks for confirmation:
That they're doing it right,
That they matter,
That they're needed. And as we grow older, this longing doesn't disappear,
It just changes its form. We want our achievements to be noticed,
We want our words to carry weight,

We want our efforts not to stay in the shadows. But here's the subtle part. When recognition becomes the only source of self-esteem, a person starts to depend on what others think. They start adjusting themselves,
Doubting,
Losing their inner compass. And then any lack of approval feels like failure. So perhaps what matters isn't giving up the desire to be recognized,
But learning to find balance.
Because outside recognition is pleasant,
But an inner sense of your own worth is far more stable. And that is what gives you real support.
